sections.headline: Earnings Season Takes Toll
sections.body: The S&P 500 fell 0.08% to 7800.62 as investors digested the mixed earnings reports from big banks and the chip sector's decline. Higher oil prices and memory chip stock losses were cited as key factors contributing to the market's subdued performance. Traders are watching for further signs of weakness in the tech sector, which has been a major driver of the market's recent gains.

sections.headline: Nasdaq Falls Amid Global AI Selloff
sections.body: The Nasdaq fell 0.19% to 27193.13 as global AI selloff intensified, with traders watching for signs of a broader tech downturn. The WSJ reported that Nasdaq futures fell due to the global AI selloff, while CNBC noted that the S&P 500 closed near flat, pressured by higher oil prices and memory chip stock losses. The chip selloff, which is also affecting the Nasdaq, is a key concern for traders, as it suggests a broader market downturn.

sections.headline: US Treasury Yields Fall Amid Market Expectations
sections.body: US Treasury yields fell 0.4% to 5.22 as markets awaited the release of US inflation data, with traders expecting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy further. [6] According to Reuters, PIMCO's Ivascyn stated that US Treasury yields are yet to peak, suggesting that the Fed may still raise interest rates. [7] The decline in yields may be attributed to the growing disconnect between the US dollar's strength and Treasury yields, as noted by FOREX.com. [8]

sections.headline: USD/JPY Rise: Geopolitical Risks and CPI
sections.body: The USD/JPY rose as traders took a cautious stance ahead of the upcoming CPI data, which may impact the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions. Geopolitical tensions and the dollar's recent strength also contributed to the move. Traders are watching for any signs of a shift in the market's sentiment towards the dollar, [11].

sections.headline: Crude Oil Prices Rise Amid Supply Concerns

Traders are watching the situation closely, as elevated crude prices could enhance ExxonMobil's cash flows, as reported by The Globe and Mail [14]. However, the recent fall in oil prices may have been due to traders assessing Russian diesel supply prospects and the Saudi-Houthi conflict, as seen on CNBC [15].
